title: The shared Temporal platform has no row in the services table, so the platform login, the task queue, the owner of the backup and restore right, the archive container immutability period and the approved server and SDK release are named by no read source
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md §R4 (19 services, no platform row); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 23, 24 and 44; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (jobs JOB-21, JOB-22 own PLT, no platform login or backup owner)
section: §3 Preconditions; §10 Authority; §13 Configuration and reference data
description: §R4 gives each of the 19 services a schema, a login, a REST base, a topic, a task queue and a Java package, and gives the shared platform no row at all. The platform is therefore described by its namespace and its work, not by an identity: no read source names the login that runs the archive run and the drills, the provisioning record of task queue `rwb-platform`, the role or team that owns the point-in-time restore right and the backup window on the flexible server, the write-once (immutability) period of the Blob container `rwb-temporal-archive`, or the approved server release and the SDK release that the upgrade drill pins. The legacy story carries the same values as assumptions (retention 30 days, archive lead time 7 days, 02:00, three retries, a backup window of at least 35 days) but names no identity and no immutability period, so the values that are fixed stay fixed and only the unstated ones are raised.
evidence: RWB-E2-039 §3 (the backup window, the immutability period and the approved release are each written as 'assumed' with no owner) and §13 (the container, its write-once period and the release 'recorded in Environment and Deployment Design v4'); Architecture v5 slide 44 puts JOB-21 and JOB-22 with owner 'platform' and no login; the Ownership Map resolves JOB-21 and JOB-22 to PLT and resolves no platform login, no platform task queue provisioning record and no backup or restore owner
proposed: Publish one platform identity section in the Wave 0 Service Catalog and the Ownership Map: the platform login and its grants, the provisioning record of task queue `rwb-platform` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, the role that owns the flexible-server backup window and the restore right, the immutability period of `rwb-temporal-archive`, and the approved Temporal server and SDK release. Until it is published the story uses the working read of ASM-B-PLT-WF-02-E2039-APP-1 and writes the placeholder wherever the value is still open.

title: The platform has no service row, and the archive immutability period, the retry count owner, the manifest retention and the approved release the version check compares against are named by no read source
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 039 Temporal resilience backup failover upgrade and archive v1.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epic 2 v2.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md
description: Template and Rules §R4 lists 19 services and has no platform row, so no read source fixes the platform identity that runs the resilience contract, and no read source names the archive immutability period, the role that owns the retry count, the manifest retention or the approved release the version step check compares the proposed target against.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-039 section 3 gives the container rwb-temporal-archive with a write-once policy for the archive period, retention 30 days (assumed, DL26), an archive lead time of 7 days (assumed) and a retry count of three, but no immutability period, no owner of the retry count and no manifest retention; section 13 records the approved server version in Environment and Deployment Design v4 without naming the approved release. Template and Rules §R4 gives the platform as wave 0 with no service short, schema, topic, queue or REST base. The Architecture v5 extract gives the one cluster per environment on ACE AKS and the upgrade from 1.28.1 to 1.30 or later; the Temporal and Drools design gives the namespace rwb-recovery and retention 30 days for closed workflows archived to Blob (E2-039); neither gives the four values.
area: Platform identity and Temporal resilience contract
proposed: Publish the platform identity and the four values once, in the Wave 0 Service Catalog and the parameters contract: the archive immutability period, the owner of the retry count, the manifest retention and the approved release the version step check compares against. This contract then reads them from there and the placeholders are replaced without a document version.

title: The platform login, the gate's pipeline identity, the owner of the replay container's retention and the pinned SDK release the gate runs at are named by no read source
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 §R4; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20, 23 and 24; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 27 notes and slide 32 item 6; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 040 Workflow versioning and replay test gate v1.md
description: Template and Rules §R4 gives a login, a schema, a REST base, a topic and a task queue to the 19 services only, and the workflow platform has no row there, so the platform has no service identity of its own and no rule that would name one. The legacy story requires a platform worker polling the platform task queue, a replay gate that runs in the pipeline against a pinned workflow SDK, and a Blob container with a 90-day retention, but no read source names the platform login that runs the export, the pipeline identity that runs the gate, the role that owns the replay container's retention policy, or the SDK release the gate is pinned to. The story uses what the sources do state as the working read of the assumption: namespace rwb-recovery, task queue `rwb-platform`, SIT histories only, 200 histories per type, a 01:00 nightly export, a 90-day retention and the legacy budgets of 24 hours freshness, 10 minutes and 60 seconds unchanged, with Temporal 1.30 or later as the floor because Worker Versioning needs it.
evidence: Template and Rules §R4 (19 service rows and no platform row, so no platform short, login, base or queue); Architecture v5 slide 20 (every service: own schema and own task queue; shared platform carries the library); slide 23 (Workflow Versioning and the versioned workflow kit owned by the platform team); slide 24 (one cluster, a namespace per workbench, a queue per service); Temporal and Drools Design slide 27 notes (Worker Versioning needs Temporal 1.30+, the replay gate replays recorded histories against every new build before release, retention 30 days with an archive to Blob) and slide 32 item 6 (Temporal 1.30+ for Nexus and Worker Versioning, no Quartz); legacy RWB-E2-040 section 3 (test kit at the pinned SDK version, Blob container with 90-day retention) names no release number, no login and no retention owner.
proposed: Fix the platform login, the pipeline identity of the gate, the owner of the replay container retention and the pinned workflow SDK release in the Wave 0 Service Catalog and the Environment and Deployment Design, and record them in the Ownership Map

title: The platform has no service row, and the pipeline identity, the replay container retention, the pinned SDK version and the build registry owner are named by no read source
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 §R4 and §R5.5 DP-10; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 040 Workflow versioning and replay test gate v1.md sections 3, 12 and 13; RWB PLT E1070 CON and RWB PLT E1071 CON
section: 1. Story; 3. Preconditions; 11. Data; 12.5 Workflows and activities; 13. Solution plan; 14. Validation and messages
description: Template and Rules §R4 defines the short, the schema, the REST base, the topic and the task queue for the 19 services only and has no platform row, so the workflow platform has no service identity of its own. Four values the replay-gate contract depends on are named by no read source: the pipeline identity that runs gate 10, the replay container retention (the legacy names 90 days and no platform source confirms it), the pinned Temporal Java SDK version the replay corpus is replayed at, and the owner of the build registry. The story publishes the working read of the assumption instead: namespace rwb-recovery, task queue `rwb-platform`, SIT-only histories, 200 closed histories per workflow type, 24-hour freshness, 10-minute gate budget, 90-day retention, gate 10 as the tenth pipeline check and MSG-P3-038 unchanged.
evidence: Template and Rules §R4 (19 service rows and no platform row); legacy RWB-E2-040 section 3 (SIT namespace rwb-recovery, Blob container rwb-temporal-replay with a 90-day retention, the SDK test kit on the test classpath at the pinned SDK version) and section 13 (200 histories per type, 24-hour freshness, 10-minute gate budget, 90-day retention); Architecture v5 slides 23 and 24 (cluster version 1.30 or later, Worker Versioning, one namespace per workbench); Ownership Map v1 (JOB-21 and JOB-22 owned by PLT and no history export job row); RWB PLT E1070 CON and RWB PLT E1071 CON state the namespace and the platform task queue only
area: Platform identity and replay gate contract
proposed: Fix the pipeline identity, the replay container retention, the pinned SDK version and the owner of the build registry in the Wave 0 Service Catalog, and record them in the Ownership Map and the Environment and Deployment Design

title: The platform has no service row, and the platform login, the quotas, the rate limits, the namespace certificate set, the key rotation period and the exact retention of the namespace are named by no read source
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 §R4 (19 service rows and no platform row) and §R5.5 DP-02 and DP-13; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8 (Key Vault, codec server, payload keys AES-GCM), 23 (L2 namespaces: own retention, quotas, certificates and codec keys), 24 (codec AES-GCM with keys in Key Vault per namespace; one task queue per service), 35 (Temporal payload codec AES-GCM with keys in Key Vault, namespaces with their own certificates and codec keys), 46 (a new workbench takes a namespace); Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 11 (AES-GCM, keys in Key Vault per namespace; UI: RW-PLATADM operate, RW-AUDIT read, RW-SECADM decode break-glass), 12 (L2 namespaces with own retention, rate limits, certificates and encryption keys), 27 (search attributes CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup, QueueCode only; retention 30 days for closed workflows, archived to Blob), 32 item 6 (Temporal 1.30 or later)
section: 1. Story; 3. Preconditions; 9. State transitions; 10. Authority; 11. Data; 13. Solution plan settings and build steps
description: Template and Rules §R4 defines the short, the schema, the REST base, the topic and the task queue for the 19 services only and has no platform row, so the shared Temporal namespace has no service identity of its own and no source fixes the values that identity would carry. Six values the namespace record depends on are named by no read source: the platform's own login and admin base, the per-namespace quotas, the per-namespace rate limits, the namespace's certificate set beyond the frontend certificate the contract profile declares, the key rotation period and version policy, and the exact retention the namespace must carry beyond the 30-day closed-workflow rule. The story provisions the namespace and the key from the working read of the assumption (namespace `rwb-recovery`, identity SY-CASEWF, one AES-GCM key per namespace in Key Vault, 30-day closed-workflow retention, RW-PLATADM operate, RW-AUDIT read, RW-SECADM decode under break-glass) and keeps the placeholder wherever a value is still open, so no number is invented to fill the record.
evidence: Template and Rules §R4: the service table has 19 rows and the platform wave-0 and integration list names epics, codes and service names but no platform service short, schema, topic, REST base or task queue; Architecture v5 slide 23: L2 namespaces 'ace-collection · rwb-recovery · next workbench: own retention, quotas, certificates and codec keys'; slide 24: 'Codec (AES-GCM, Key Vault) on every client and worker; codec server for the UI' and 'keys in Key Vault per namespace'; slide 35: 'Temporal payload codec encrypts payloads (AES-GCM) with keys in Key Vault' and 'Temporal namespaces have their own certificates and codec keys'; slide 46: a new workbench is a new namespace, not a new cluster; Temporal and Drools Design slide 11: 'Payloads encrypted by the codec (AES-GCM, keys in Key Vault per namespace). Temporal UI behind Entra ID; RW-PLATADM operate, RW-AUDIT read, RW-SECADM decode (break-glass)'; slide 12 note: 'one per workbench (ace-collection, rwb-recovery, the next one), each with its own retention, rate limits, certificates and encryption keys'; slide 27 note: 'search attributes are CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup, QueueCode only ... Retention 30 days for closed workflows, archived to Blob'; slide 32 item 6: 'Temporal 1.30+ for Nexus and Worker Versioning'; no read source states a platform login, admin base, quota value, rate-limit value, key rotation period or certificate list
proposed: Fix the platform identity and admin base, the per-namespace quotas and rate limits, the namespace certificate set, the key rotation period and version policy, and the exact retention the namespace carries in the Wave 0 Service Catalog and the platform run book, then record them in the Ownership Map and the Environment and Deployment Design

title: The baseline parameters of a moved non-functional story are named by no read source beyond 1.30 or later and the ACE objectives
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 §R6 (No impact rows: moved to their epic with content unchanged) and §R4 (19 service rows and no platform row); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 23 (five layers; version 1.30+; one cluster per environment, namespace per workbench, one queue per service; payload codec AES-GCM; Continue-As-New at stage ends), 24 (codec AES-GCM with keys in Key Vault per namespace; KEDA per queue), 35 (mTLS, per-service ACLs, namespaces with their own certificates and codec keys), 46 (namespace, not a cluster, for the next workbench); Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 12 (the five layers and their owners), 13 (Continue-As-New at each stage end, at least every 28 days; parent close policy ABANDON), 27 (deterministic workflow code; Worker Versioning and getVersion; replay gate; AES-GCM codec; search attributes; retention 30 days archived to Blob), 32 item 6 (Temporal 1.30+ for Nexus and Worker Versioning, no Quartz); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 §6.4 NFR-020, NFR-021, NFR-022, NFR-023 and §6.7 NFR-045
section: 1. Story; 3. Preconditions; 9. State transitions; 10. Authority; 12.6 Schedules; 13. Solution plan settings
description: NF-08 is a non-functional statement that is moved to its epic with content unchanged, and the baseline record it becomes must carry parameters that no read source fixes: the exact supported version range beyond the 1.30-or-later family, the full compatibility matrix of server, SDK and schema tool, the upgrade cadence and the upgrade window, the measurement window of the availability and recovery objectives, and the conformance cadence. Template and Rules §R4 also has no platform row, so the record has no service identity of its own to derive them from. The story publishes the working read of the assumption (1.30 or later with the ACE recovery objectives and one conformance run per release) and keeps the placeholder on every parameter that is still open, so the record does not present an invented number as a standard.
evidence: Template and Rules §R6: the No impact list moves E1-024, E1-025, E1-026, E1-033, E1-034, E1-038, E1-040, E1-041, E1-045, E1-053, E1-060, E1-061, E1-068 and TE-010 and TE-012 'to their epic with content unchanged'; §R4: the service table has 19 rows and no platform row; Architecture v5 slide 23: 'Upgrade from 1.28.1 to 1.30 or later for Nexus and Worker Versioning' and the four reusable rules (no business terms in L1 to L3 interfaces, kit versioned with workers pinned, all I/O in activities with Continue-As-New at stage ends, payloads encrypted by the codec); slide 46: 'a new workbench is a new namespace, not a new cluster'; Temporal and Drools Design slide 27 note: 'Worker Versioning (workers pinned to a build; needs Temporal 1.30+, v5 slide 23), Workflow.getVersion(...) for in-place code changes, and the replay gate (E2-040, MSG-P3-038)'; slide 32 item 6: 'Temporal 1.30+, jobs as Schedules ... Nexus, Worker Versioning; no Quartz'; Program BRD v4 NFR-020 and NFR-021 set 99.9 percent in business hours and 99.5 percent outside them, NFR-022 and NFR-023 are Open and follow the ACE recovery objectives; no read source states the supported range, the matrix, the upgrade cadence, the upgrade window, the measurement window or the conformance cadence
proposed: Fix the supported version range, the full compatibility matrix, the upgrade cadence and window, the measurement window of the availability and recovery objectives and the conformance cadence at the platform infrastructure review, and record them in the Environment and Deployment Design, the Service Catalog and the baseline record before wave 0 exit
